Spike-in vs No Spike-in vs Literature: Significant mRNA Counts (Lollipop Charts)

Kate

2026-07-20

Purpose

Second notebook in the spike-in vs literature comparison subsection. Part 1 re-renders 01_lollipop_sig_genes_spike_vs_nospike.Rmd’s significant-gene counts as horizontal bar charts (flipped orientation from 01’s vertical bars), reusing 01’s already-saved output with no recomputation. Part 2 documents candidate published ribosome profiling / translation-efficiency hypoxia datasets located for comparison — these are not yet plotted, pending Kate’s decision on which are actually comparable (see caveats noted per dataset below).

Part 1: Lollipop version of notebook 01

Load 01’s saved significant-gene counts

No recomputation here — 01_lollipop_sig_genes_spike_vs_nospike.Rmd already computed and saved these counts (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5, sictrl hypoxia vs normoxia, RNA/Ribo/TE, with vs without spike-in, at 1/4/24hr) to output/spikein_literature_comparison/01_sig_gene_counts_spike_vs_nospike.csv.

sig_counts_file <- here("output/spikein_literature_comparison/01_sig_gene_counts_spike_vs_nospike.csv")
stopifnot("01_sig_gene_counts_spike_vs_nospike.csv missing — knit 01 first" = file.exists(sig_counts_file))

sig_counts_long <- read_csv(sig_counts_file, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(
    Timepoint = factor(Timepoint, levels = c("1hr", "4hr", "24hr")),
    Direction = factor(Direction, levels = c("Up", "Down")),
    Mode = factor(Mode, levels = c("RNA", "Ribo", "TE"))
  )

modes <- levels(sig_counts_long$Mode)
print(sig_counts_long)

Bar charts (one per mode: RNA, Ribo, TE)

Same information as before (Up = Okabe-Ito vermillion, Down = Okabe-Ito dark blue; with spike-in = full saturation, no spike-in = a lighter tint of the same hue; faceted by timepoint; dodged by spike-in status), but drawn as horizontal bars instead of lollipops: Direction now sits on the y-axis and the count runs left to right on the x-axis (flipped from the original vertical orientation).

up_dark <- "#D55E00"
down_dark <- "#0072B2"
lighten <- function(hex, amount = 0.55) colorRampPalette(c(hex, "white"))(101)[round(amount * 100) + 1]
up_light <- lighten(up_dark)
down_light <- lighten(down_dark)

color_values <- c(
  "Up - With spike-in" = up_dark,
  "Up - No spike-in" = up_light,
  "Down - With spike-in" = down_dark,
  "Down - No spike-in" = down_light
)

make_bar <- function(df, mode_label) {
  plot_df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      color_group = factor(paste(Direction, spike_status, sep = " - "), levels = names(color_values)),
      spike_status = factor(spike_status, levels = c("No spike-in", "With spike-in"))
    )

  dodge <- position_dodge(width = 0.7)
  x_max <- 9000

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(y = Direction, x = n, fill = color_group)) +
    geom_col(position = dodge, width = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), position = dodge, hjust = -0.2, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = color_values) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, x_max * 1.15)) +
    facet_wrap(~Timepoint, nrow = 1) +
    labs(title = paste0(mode_label, " sig genes: sictrl hypoxia vs normoxia"),
         x = "# sig genes (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 0.5)", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          axis.line.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.line.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          strip.background = element_blank(),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 15))
}

bar_plots <- setNames(lapply(modes, function(m) {
  make_bar(sig_counts_long %>% filter(Mode == m), m)
}), modes)

bar_plots[["RNA"]]

ggsave(here("plots/02_bar_sig_rna_spike_vs_nospike.pdf"), plot = bar_plots[["RNA"]], width = 7, height = 4.5)

Part 2: Candidate literature ribosome-profiling hypoxia datasets

Status: research only, nothing plotted yet. These are candidates located for Kate to review; inclusion depends on her judgment about comparability to our own condition (MDA-MB-231, sictrl, hypoxia vs normoxia, 1/4/24hr — exact O2% and chamber duration for our own experiment were not found documented anywhere in this repo and need to be confirmed before any “same condition” claims are made in a figure). Citations use Author et al. YYYY format per Kate’s request, to sit alongside our own “Pre spike-in” / “Post spike-in” bars in a future combined plot.

Citation Journal Cell line O2% hypoxia (vs normoxia) Duration(s) Method Reported sig. gene/mRNA counts Comparability notes
Jiang et al. 2017 BMC Genomics ARPE-19 (human retinal pigment epithelium) 1% (vs 21%) 1h, 2h, 4h Ribo-seq + RNA-seq, DTG/DTE (fold-change > 2 based cutoffs, not padj) Up-regulated DTGs: 128 (1h), 183 (2h), 293 (4h); differential-TE mRNA counts: 419 (1h), 239 (2h), 158 (4h) — paper does not cleanly separate down-regulated counts from up in the summary text; would need table/supplement pull to get Down Best timepoint match to ours (1h/4h). Non-cancer cell line. Different DE method/cutoffs (FC>2, not padj<0.05 &
Ho et al. 2016 Cell Reports (10.1016/j.celrep.2016.01.036) U87MG (glioblastoma), 786-O (renal clear cell carcinoma) 1% (vs 21%) 24h (+ 6h pretreatment/24h labeling variant) Ribosome-footprint profiling + quantitative MS No up/down significant-gene counts reported in the padj/FC-cutoff sense used here — genes instead binned into Class I/II/III translation-efficiency-ratio categories (25%/60%/~15%) Duration matches our 24h timepoint well. Not a compatible summary statistic (no discrete “N up / N down” figure) — would need raw data reprocessing to get a comparable count, not just a citation.
Ho et al. 2020 Nature Communications (10.1038/s41467-020-16504-1) U87MG (glioblastoma) 1% (0.1% used only in a C. elegans validation arm) 24h primary, 72h confirmatory Polysome profiling + TMT-pSILAC + RNA-seq (not ribo-seq) HuR-knockdown-dependent: ~3,435 mRNAs affected at TE level vs. 1,323 at RNA level (2-fold threshold) — this is an RBP-knockdown effect, not a plain hypoxia-vs-normoxia comparison Different assay (polysome profiling, not ribo-seq) and different comparison (HuR KD, not hypoxia vs normoxia) — weakest match of the four; flagging mainly because it’s from the same group/cell line as Ho et al. 2016.
Andreev et al. 2015 Genome Biology (10.1186/s13059-015-0651-z) PC12 (rat pheochromocytoma, neural) 0% O2 (anoxia) + glucose deprivation, vs 21% O2 20min, 40min, 1h, 2h, 4h Ribo-seq, Z-score + 10% FDR At 40 min: 3,202 DE genes by ribo-seq occupancy; 2,556 DE genes by TE — up/down not separated in the summary; other timepoints not fully extracted here Oxygen-glucose deprivation (OGD), not pure hypoxia — confounded by glucose withdrawal. Anoxia (0% O2) is far more severe than typical 1% hypoxia protocols. Different species (rat) and cell type (neural, not epithelial/cancer). Weak match on condition despite good ribo-seq method match.

Not pursued further / lower priority: - Erhard et al. 2025 (Nat Commun, HIF1α nucleolar ribosome biogenesis, breast cancer, 1% vs 20% O2) — breast-cancer relevant and O2% plausibly comparable, but the paper’s focus is rRNA transcription/ribosome biogenesis, not a ribo-seq TE up/down gene-count comparison; would need a closer read of methods/supplement to see if a comparable count exists. - van den Beucken et al. (RNA-binding-protein/anaerobic-metabolism hypoxia translation work) — repeatedly surfaced in searches but could not confirm a ribo-seq-based up/down significant-gene count in the time spent; flagging the author/topic in case Kate recognizes the specific paper she has in mind.

Resolved: our own hypoxia condition is 1% O2, chamber duration = the sample timepoint itself (1/4/24hr). Confirmed by Kate; not documented anywhere in this repo prior to this notebook. Under this condition, Jiang et al. 2017 (1% O2, 1h/2h/4h) is the closest O2%/duration match among the candidates above.

Part 3: Hettiarachchi et al. 2019 comparison (human primary hepatocytes)

Hettiarachchi GK, et al. “Translational and transcriptional responses in human primary hepatocytes under hypoxia.” Am J Physiol Gastrointest Liver Physiol 2019. DOI: 10.1152/ajpgi.00331.2018 (PMC6620582).

  • Cell type: pooled human primary hepatocytes from 5 donors (Thermo Fisher Scientific), mixed age/sex/phenotype.
  • O2%: 1% hypoxia vs. ambient (~21%) normoxia — matches our own condition exactly.
  • Timepoints: 30 min and 240 min of hypoxia exposure (chamber: Plas-Labs glove box, 37°C). 240 min = 4hr matches our 4hr timepoint exactly. 30 min does not correspond exactly to any of our timepoints (our earliest is 1hr = 60min) — noted, not silently aligned.
  • Method: RNA-seq + Ribo-seq + TE (ratio of ribosome-protected fragments to mRNA fragments), matching our own assay type.
  • Their own significance cutoffs: |log2FC| > 1 and padj (BH-FDR) < 0.10 — looser padj, stricter LFC than ours (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5).
  • Their reported totals (Fig. in paper, not split by up/down): 760 differential-TE genes at 30 min; 841 at 240 min.
  • Supplied by Kate: accessories/hettiarachchi riboseq/supplemental file s1.xls, with per-comparison tabs including "0 vs 30 min TE" and "0 vs 240 min TE".
library(readxl)
## Warning: package 'readxl' was built under R version 4.3.3
hetti_file <- here("accessories", "hettiarachchi riboseq", "supplemental file s1.xls")
stopifnot("Hettiarachchi supplemental file not found" = file.exists(hetti_file))

hetti_sheets <- c("30min" = "0 vs 30 min TE", "240min" = "0 vs 240 min TE")

hetti_te <- lapply(hetti_sheets, function(sheet) {
  read_excel(hetti_file, sheet = sheet) %>%
    dplyr::rename(symbol = 1)
})
## New names:
## New names:
## • `` -> `...1`
for (tp in names(hetti_te)) {
  cat(tp, "TE sheet rows:", nrow(hetti_te[[tp]]), "\n")
}
## 30min TE sheet rows: 760 
## 240min TE sheet rows: 841

Important caveat: the supplied TE tabs are already pre-filtered to the authors’ own significant gene set

for (tp in names(hetti_te)) {
  d <- hetti_te[[tp]]
  stopifnot(
    "Expected every row to already pass the paper's own |log2FC| > 1 cutoff" =
      all(abs(d$log2FoldChange) > 1, na.rm = TRUE),
    "Expected every row to already pass the paper's own padj < 0.10 cutoff" =
      all(d$padj < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
}
cat("Confirmed: both TE tabs contain only the", nrow(hetti_te[["30min"]]),
    "/", nrow(hetti_te[["240min"]]), "genes the authors themselves called\n")
## Confirmed: both TE tabs contain only the 760 / 841 genes the authors themselves called
cat("significant (|log2FC| > 1, padj < 0.10) — NOT the full genome-wide DESeq2 output.\n")
## significant (|log2FC| > 1, padj < 0.10) — NOT the full genome-wide DESeq2 output.

Row counts (760, 841) match the paper’s reported totals exactly, confirming these tabs are the authors’ final significant-gene lists, not unfiltered results. Consequence: applying our own thresholds below only re-filters within this already-significant set. Any gene with 0.5 <= |log2FC| < 1 that would have passed our padj < 0.05 cutoff on the full dataset is absent from this file entirely — so the counts below are a lower bound, not the true count we’d get from the full unfiltered Hettiarachchi et al. DESeq2 results (which were not supplied).

Reproducibility check: applying their exact cutoffs to their own data reproduces their reported totals

paper_reported_total <- c("30min" = 760, "240min" = 841)

for (tp in names(hetti_te)) {
  d <- hetti_te[[tp]]
  n_matching_their_cutoffs <- sum(abs(d$log2FoldChange) > 1 & d$padj < 0.10, na.rm = TRUE)
  cat(tp, ": applying |log2FC| > 1 & padj < 0.10 to their data gives",
      n_matching_their_cutoffs, "genes (they reported", paper_reported_total[[tp]], ")\n")
  stopifnot(
    "Reapplying the paper's own cutoffs to their own data did not reproduce their reported total" =
      n_matching_their_cutoffs == paper_reported_total[[tp]]
  )
}
## 30min : applying |log2FC| > 1 & padj < 0.10 to their data gives 760 genes (they reported 760 )
## 240min : applying |log2FC| > 1 & padj < 0.10 to their data gives 841 genes (they reported 841 )
cat("Confirmed: their cutoffs reproduce their reported totals exactly at both timepoints.\n")
## Confirmed: their cutoffs reproduce their reported totals exactly at both timepoints.

Apply our thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5) and compare to their reported totals

count_sig_hetti <- function(d) {
  sig <- d %>% filter(!is.na(padj), padj < 0.05, abs(log2FoldChange) >= 0.5)
  tibble(Up = sum(sig$log2FoldChange > 0), Down = sum(sig$log2FoldChange < 0))
}

hetti_counts <- map_dfr(names(hetti_te), function(tp) {
  count_sig_hetti(hetti_te[[tp]]) %>% mutate(Timepoint = tp)
}) %>%
  mutate(Our_threshold_total = Up + Down)

hetti_comparison <- hetti_counts %>%
  mutate(
    Paper_reported_total = c(`30min` = 760, `240min` = 841)[Timepoint],
    Paper_cutoffs = "|log2FC| > 1, padj < 0.10 (not split by direction)"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Timepoint, Up, Down, Our_threshold_total, Paper_reported_total, Paper_cutoffs)

print(hetti_comparison)
## # A tibble: 2 × 6
##   Timepoint    Up  Down Our_threshold_total Paper_reported_total Paper_cutoffs  
##   <chr>     <int> <int>               <int>                <dbl> <chr>          
## 1 30min       359   262                 621                  760 |log2FC| > 1, …
## 2 240min      278   345                 623                  841 |log2FC| > 1, …
write_csv(hetti_comparison, here("output/spikein_literature_comparison/02_hettiarachchi_te_comparison.csv"))
cat("Saved Hettiarachchi et al. 2019 TE comparison to output/spikein_literature_comparison/\n")
## Saved Hettiarachchi et al. 2019 TE comparison to output/spikein_literature_comparison/

Our-threshold total will be <= the paper’s reported total at each timepoint (subset of an already-filtered set, per the caveat above) — this is expected and not evidence of a discrepancy in either analysis.

Part 4: TE comparison (1/4/24hr) — with spike-in vs no spike-in vs Hettiarachchi et al. 2019

Reorganized to match the layout used for the final combined plot in 04_bar_te_si3d_si3e_with_nospike_vs_literature.Rmd: source labels on the x-axis, bars going up (count on the y-axis), axis text rotated 90° and wrapped, dotted/dashed vertical separators grouping the categories instead of interleaving them.

Left to right: with spike-in, all three timepoints (1hr, 4hr, 24hr) — one set of Up/Down bars per timepoint — then a dotted vertical line, then no spike-in, all three timepoints — another set of Up/Down bars per timepoint (6 “ours” sets total), then a dashed vertical line, then Hettiarachchi et al. 2019’s own Up/Down counts, in order of the hypoxia timepoint used (30min, then 240min). Unlike the previous version of this plot, our three timepoints are no longer individually paired against a matched Hettiarachchi timepoint — all “ours” bars are grouped together, all literature bars are grouped together, same as notebook 04.

All “ours” counts use our thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5), not the original publication’s cutoffs — the Hettiarachchi bars remain a lower bound (see Part 3 caveat) since their supplied data was pre-filtered under their own looser/stricter mixed cutoffs before we ever applied ours. The Hettiarachchi counts reused here (hetti_counts, from Part 3) were already reproducibility-checked against the paper’s own reported totals in the hetti_reproduce_their_totals chunk above (760 at 30min, 841 at 240min, both stopifnot-verified) — this section adds no new, unchecked Hettiarachchi numbers. Our 24hr timepoint has no Hettiarachchi match (the paper only reports 30min/240min) — it still gets its own with-spike/no-spike bars in the “ours” block, just no literature counterpart.

Bar fill follows notebook 04’s convention: “ours” bars (all six) share one Okabe-Ito color, literature bars are grey; Up/Down is conveyed by the bold vermillion/blue count label above each bar, not by fill.

ours_color <- "#009E73"
literature_color <- "grey50"

our_te_all <- sig_counts_long %>%
  filter(Mode == "TE") %>%
  mutate(spike_status = factor(spike_status, levels = c("With spike-in", "No spike-in"))) %>%
  transmute(
    source = paste0("**", spike_status, " (", Timepoint, ")**"),
    Direction, n, spike_status, Timepoint
  )

hetti_30min_long <- hetti_counts %>%
  filter(Timepoint == "30min") %>%
  dplyr::select(Up, Down) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Direction", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(source = "Hettiarachchi et al. 2019<br>(30min, 1% O2,<br>human primary hepatocytes)")

hetti_240min_long <- hetti_counts %>%
  filter(Timepoint == "240min") %>%
  dplyr::select(Up, Down) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "Direction", values_to = "n") %>%
  mutate(source = "Hettiarachchi et al. 2019<br>(240min/4hr, 1% O2,<br>human primary hepatocytes)")

source_levels <- c(
  "**With spike-in (1hr)**", "**With spike-in (4hr)**", "**With spike-in (24hr)**",
  "**No spike-in (1hr)**", "**No spike-in (4hr)**", "**No spike-in (24hr)**",
  "Hettiarachchi et al. 2019<br>(30min, 1% O2,<br>human primary hepatocytes)",
  "Hettiarachchi et al. 2019<br>(240min/4hr, 1% O2,<br>human primary hepatocytes)"
)

n_ours <- 6
n_with_spike <- 3

source_colors <- setNames(
  c(rep(ours_color, n_ours), rep(literature_color, length(source_levels) - n_ours)),
  source_levels
)

te_vs_hetti <- bind_rows(
  our_te_all %>% dplyr::select(source, Direction, n),
  hetti_30min_long %>% dplyr::select(source, Direction, n),
  hetti_240min_long %>% dplyr::select(source, Direction, n)
) %>%
  mutate(
    Direction = factor(Direction, levels = c("Up", "Down")),
    source = factor(source, levels = source_levels)
  )

print(te_vs_hetti)

library(ggtext)

y_pad <- 0.20 * max(te_vs_hetti$n)

Part 5: RNA & Ribo comparison vs Shen et al. 2020 (hypoxic rat cardiomyocytes)

Shen JJ, et al. “Translatome and Transcriptome Profiling of Hypoxic-Induced Rat Cardiomyocytes.” Molecular Therapy Nucleic Acids 2020. DOI: 10.1016/j.omtn.2020.09.010 (PMC7689039).

Unlike Part 4 (TE), this comparison uses RNA and Ribo separately (ours, 4hr only — the closest of our timepoints to Shen et al.’s 8h — with and without spike-in) against Shen et al.’s RNA-seq (transcriptome) and polyribo-seq (translatome) DEG counts — matching metric to metric instead of comparing TE to a non-TE metric. Only the 8h vs normoxia comparison is used for both RNA-seq and Ribo-seq (a true hypoxia-vs-normoxia comparison, like ours); the paper’s 24h-vs-8h comparisons (severe vs. mild hypoxia, NOT vs. normoxia — see prior discussion) are excluded from this plot entirely, for both modalities, since that isn’t the comparison type this plot is built around.

  • Cell type: rat cardiac myoblast H9C2 cell line (in vitro; the paper’s in vivo rat left-ventricle arm is not used here).
  • O2%: 1% O2 (94% N2, 5% CO2) vs standard culture normoxia.
  • Timepoint: 8h hypoxia. Not an exact match to our 4hr timepoint (longer).
  • No spike-in normalization used. Confirmed directly: Shen et al. quantify with StringTie FPKM values and call differential expression with Ballgown — no ERCC or exogenous RNA spike-ins anywhere in their pipeline. So every Shen et al. bar in this plot is effectively a “no spike-in” condition, unlike our own bars (which show both).
  • Their cutoffs: |log2FC| >= 1 and raw p < 0.05 (Ballgown, not BH-adjusted padj) — looser statistical correction than ours (padj < 0.05).
  • No supplementary per-gene file used for a re-filter under our own cutoffs. Ballgown’s output does not report an lfcSE column, so even with the raw supplementary tables (Table S3 = RNA-seq, Table S4 = polyribo-seq DEGs) there is no valid way to propagate error into a padj for a derived quantity — the counts below are the paper’s own reported totals, taken as-is, not recomputed under our thresholds.
shen_groups <- tribble(
  ~source, ~Direction, ~n,
  "Shen et al. 2020<br>(H9C2, RNA-seq, 8hr, 1% O2, |log2FC| >= 1, p < 0.05)", "Up", 1527,
  "Shen et al. 2020<br>(H9C2, RNA-seq, 8hr, 1% O2, |log2FC| >= 1, p < 0.05)", "Down", 1398,
  "Shen et al. 2020<br>(H9C2, Ribo-seq, 8hr, 1% O2, |log2FC| >= 1, p < 0.05)", "Up", 536,
  "Shen et al. 2020<br>(H9C2, Ribo-seq, 8hr, 1% O2, |log2FC| >= 1, p < 0.05)", "Down", 429
)

our_rna_ribo <- sig_counts_long %>%
  filter(Mode %in% c("RNA", "Ribo"), Timepoint == "4hr") %>%
  transmute(
    modality = as.character(Mode),
    source = paste0("**", Mode, ": ", spike_status, " (", Timepoint, ")**"),
    Direction, n
  )

rna_source_levels <- c(
  "**RNA: With spike-in (4hr)**", "**RNA: No spike-in (4hr)**",
  "Shen et al. 2020<br>(H9C2, RNA-seq, 8hr, 1% O2, |log2FC| >= 1, p < 0.05)"
)
ribo_source_levels <- c(

  "Shen et al. 2020<br>(H9C2, Ribo-seq, 8hr, 1% O2, |log2FC| >= 1, p < 0.05)"
)

rna_vs_shen <- bind_rows(
  our_rna_ribo %>% filter(modality == "RNA") %>% dplyr::select(source, Direction, n),
  shen_groups %>% filter(grepl("RNA-seq", source))
) %>%
  mutate(Direction = factor(Direction, levels = c("Up", "Down")),
         source = factor(source, levels = rna_source_levels))

  our_rna_ribo %>% filter(modality == "Ribo") %>% dplyr::select(source, Direction, n),
  shen_groups %>% filter(grepl("Ribo-seq", source))
) %>%
  mutate(Direction = factor(Direction, levels = c("Up", "Down")),

make_rna_ribo_bar <- function(df, source_levels_local, modality_label) {
  x_pad_local <- 0.15 * max(df$n)
  ggplot(df, aes(y = source, x = n, fill = Direction)) +
    geom_col(position = dodge, width = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n), position = dodge, hjust = -0.25, size = 3.5, fontface = "bold") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linewidth = 1) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Up = up_dark, Down = down_dark)) +
    scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, max(df$n) + x_pad_local)) +
    scale_y_discrete(limits = rev(source_levels_local)) +
    labs(title = paste0(modality_label, " changes: ours (with/without spike-in, 1hr & 4hr) vs Shen et al. 2020"),
         subtitle = "Ours uses OUR cutoffs (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5). Shen et al. counts are their own reported MH-vs-NC totals (|log2FC| >= 1, raw p < 0.05), not recomputed under our cutoffs.",
         x = "# sig genes", y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
    theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 8.5),
          axis.line.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.x = element_line(linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.line.y = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_markdown(size = 9.5))
}

p_rna_vs_shen <- make_rna_ribo_bar(rna_vs_shen, rna_source_levels, "RNA")
p_rna_vs_shen

ggsave(here("plots/02_bar_rna_vs_shen.pdf"), plot = p_rna_vs_shen, width = 7.5, height = 4.5)

p_ribo_vs_shen <- make_rna_ribo_bar(ribo_vs_shen, ribo_source_levels, "Ribo")
p_ribo_vs_shen

Part 6: RNA & Ribo versions of the Part 4 (TE) plot, one modality per plot

Same 04-style layout as Part 4’s TE-vs-Hettiarachchi plot (source labels on the x-axis, bars up, dotted line splitting with-spike/no-spike “ours” blocks, dashed line before literature, ours = Okabe-Ito, literature = grey) — but for RNA and Ribo instead of TE, each as its own plot rather than one combined chart, since Shen et al. 2020’s RNA-seq and Ribo-seq numbers are different modalities and don’t belong on the same “# sig genes” axis as each other (or as our TE bars). Each plot pairs our own RNA (or Ribo) with/without spike-in counts at all three timepoints (1/4/24hr) against Shen et al. 2020’s matching modality (their only reported hypoxia-vs-normoxia timepoint, 8h) — see Part 5 above for full sourcing/caveats on the Shen et al. numbers reused here.

make_ours_vs_lit_plot <- function(mode, literature_df, literature_levels, mode_label, lit_label_short) {
  ours_levels <- c(
    paste0("**With spike-in (", levels(sig_counts_long$Timepoint), ")**"),
    paste0("**No spike-in (", levels(sig_counts_long$Timepoint), ")**")
  )
  n_ours <- length(ours_levels)
  n_with_spike <- length(levels(sig_counts_long$Timepoint))

  our_data <- sig_counts_long %>%
    filter(Mode == mode) %>%
    mutate(spike_status = factor(spike_status, levels = c("With spike-in", "No spike-in"))) %>%
    transmute(source = paste0("**", spike_status, " (", Timepoint, ")**"), Direction, n)

  source_levels_local <- c(ours_levels, literature_levels)

  plot_df <- bind_rows(our_data, literature_df) %>%
    mutate(Direction = factor(Direction, levels = c("Up", "Down")),
           source = factor(source, levels = source_levels_local))

  source_colors_local <- setNames(
    c(rep(ours_color, n_ours), rep(literature_color, length(literature_levels))),
    source_levels_local
  )

  y_pad_local <- 0.20 * max(plot_df$n)
  dodge_local <- position_dodge(width = 0.7)

  ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = source, y = n, fill = source, group = Direction)) +
    geom_col(position = dodge_local, width = 0.6) +
    geom_text(aes(label = n, color = Direction), position = dodge_local,
              vjust = -0.4, size = 8, fontface = "bold", key_glyph = "point") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linewidth = 1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = n_with_spike + 0.5, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.7, color = "grey30") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = n_ours + 0.5, linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 0.7, color = "grey30") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = source_colors_local, guide = "none") +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Up = up_dark, Down = down_dark), name = NULL) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, max(plot_df$n) + y_pad_local)) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = source_levels_local) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 7))) +
    labs(title = paste0(mode_label, " changes: ours (1/4/24hr, with/without spike-in)\nvs ", lit_label_short),
         subtitle = "All counts use OUR cutoffs (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| >= 0.5), not the original publication's cutoffs.\nOurs = Okabe-Ito; literature = grey.",
         x = NULL, y = "# sig genes") +
    theme_classic(base_size = 24) +
    theme(legend.position = "top",
          legend.text = element_text(size = 21),
          plot.title = element_text(size = 25),
          plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "grey40", size = 15),
          axis.line.y = element_line(linewidth = 0.9),
          axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
          axis.text.y = element_blank(),
          axis.title.y = element_text(size = 22),
          axis.line.x = element_blank(),
          axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
          axis.text.x = element_markdown(size = 18, angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
}
